Moscow is a renter-heavy town. Only 40.0 percent of Moscow homes are lived in by their owners, a survey figure covering 2020 to 2024. The town had an estimated 26,721 residents on July 1, 2025. Turnover is high, so plenty of people selling here are landlords or heirs, not longtime occupants.

Housing measureMoscow
Population estimate, July 1, 202526,721
Households, 2020 to 202410,166
Owner-occupied housing rate40.0%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$376,400
Median gross rent$927

That median blends every owner-occupied home in town, and yours could sit far from it. A house by Paradise Creek, up on a hillside or out near the forest differs in condition and lot from a 1950s place near downtown, and buyers weigh those differences. Downtown still has commercial buildings from the 1890s.

The University of Idaho keeps Moscow supplied with renters and ties the calendar to the school year. It enrolls more than 12,000 students, over 11,000 of them on the Moscow campus, and its campus is the largest in the state.

Owners of former or current student rentals should think about three things:

  • Leases tend to track the academic year. If the buyer needs an empty house, aim your closing at a lease end.
  • Wear from renters shows up in floors, paint and kitchens. An investor planning a rehab shrugs at it, while a move-in buyer does not.
  • A tenant who stays keeps the lease terms after the sale, so reread the lease before naming a closing date.

If tenants are staying, put the lease in the buyer's hands early. Rent amount, end date and any deposit details all affect what a buyer will pay and when they can take possession. A house with a lease running into summer sells on different terms than one that is empty by May.

Cash buyers weigh the same factors as any other buyer: condition, lease status, title and repair cost.

Cold, snowy winters and dry summers put the load on the roof, the heating system and the plumbing. Expect roughly 50.9 inches of snow and 27.78 inches of total precipitation in a normal year, with snow lying on about 27 days. January lows average about 22 degrees, and the record is minus 42.

  • Check the roof for ice dam damage and worn flashing, especially on older houses.
  • Note how old the furnace is and how much insulation the attic has. Buyers ask.
  • Inspect exposed pipes and crawl spaces, where freeze damage tends to show first.

Snow can hide roof and yard problems from a buyer. If repairs are out of reach before listing, an as-is cash sale lets the buyer absorb them in the price.

Moscow is in Latah County. Early each November the treasurer mails one bill for the whole calendar year. Paying the full amount or the first half is due by December 20, with the second half following on June 20 of the next year.

Interest on a late second half is figured back to January 1, which the treasurer calls very costly. The postmark is the payment date, yet the county recommends having the post office hand cancel it, since the Postal Service no longer guarantees a postmark on all mail.

What to look for on the bill:

  • The parcel number, legal description, tax charges and any delinquencies.
  • A line labeled HO EXEMPT IMPRVMNT, which means the homeowner's exemption has been applied.
  • How the tax divides among the districts that levy it: school, city, highway, fire, library and others.

Half of a home's value, on up to one acre, is exempt for an owner who lives there, subject to a legal maximum that changes over time. The treasurer's tax bill page and the Idaho State Tax Commission's homeowner page explain how to claim it.

It follows the occupant, not the house. After a sale, a buyer who will live there files a new claim.

Moscow School District 281 serves the whole city through Moscow High School, Moscow Middle School and several elementary schools. Two public charters, Palouse Prairie Charter School and Moscow Charter School, enroll local families as well.

US 95 runs north to Coeur d'Alene and south to Lewiston and the Treasure Valley, and Idaho 8 runs east to Troy and west to Pullman. The Pullman Moscow Regional Airport is about four miles west. SMART, the Sustainable Moscow Area Transit Service, runs from the Moscow Intermodal Transit Center, and the Paradise Path gives walkers and cyclists an east to west route past the university and parks.

A property condition disclosure form is required from anyone selling a residence with up to four dwelling units, under Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it. An individually owned unit in a larger building counts too.

Use it to describe material physical problems. The statute fixes certain statements that every form carries. If you know of a leaking roof, a bad foundation or a failed septic system, write it down. Idaho Code 55-2508 contains the standard form.

Selling to us leaves that duty in place, so fill the form out honestly. What changes is that we buy as-is and do not ask you to repair what it lists.

Cash means no showings, no waiting on a buyer's loan and no repair haggling. Listing reaches more buyers and might fetch more. Your timeline and the shape of the house decide which is better.

  • List when the house is in good repair and you can sit through showings and underwriting.
  • Go cash when the house needs work, tenants are hard to relocate, or a lease end or family matter sets the date.

Our offer reflects the house as it is today. No price is promised sight unseen, and declining costs you nothing.

To get a clear offer, have these ready:

  • The address and a rough list of the repairs you are aware of.
  • Any lease, with the end date and monthly rent.
  • Your latest Latah County tax bill, so the parcel and any exemption can be confirmed.
  • Any mortgage or lien on the title.

After you accept, a title company runs the closing, settles any loan or unpaid tax out of the proceeds and pays you the balance. Early access to the lease and tax bill keeps that short.

The town occupies a valley under the Palouse Range, at the eastern edge of the Palouse and near the Washington line. Main Street is the north to south spine. Wheat fields roll around it on deep loess soil, and conifer forest begins a short drive east.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Moscow house while tenants live in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease survives the sale, so the buyer inherits the tenants' rights. Check its end date and notice terms and share them early so the offer accounts for them.

faqs.q: When are Latah County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 for the full amount or first half, June 20 for the second. A late second half accrues interest from January 1.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Moscow house before selling it for cash?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is, so an aging roof or worn floors can stay as they are. Idaho's seller disclosure form is still yours to complete.

faqs.q: Why is homeownership low in Moscow?
faqs.a: Owners occupy just 40.0 percent of homes. The University of Idaho and its big student renter population are the likely reason.

faqs.q: Does Moscow's winter affect when I should sell?
faqs.a: It can. About 50.9 inches of snow falls in a typical year and can mask roof and yard issues. Our cash offer is not seasonal, since we look at the house as it stands.
